definition_en: the degree to which something happens; the size or range of something; a limit
core_image: 一把尺子量出一件事延伸到哪里、有多深
scene: 损坏的程度仍然未知。The extent of the damage is still unknown.
sceneCN: 这里 extent 是「范围、程度」（第 2 个义项）；句意：损坏的程度仍然未知。

senses.title: Degree
senses.definition: the degree to which something happens or is true
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或成立的程度
senses.example: I agree with you to some extent.
senses.exampleCN: 我在某种程度上同意你。
senses.why: The core sense is how far a quality reaches.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是某种性质延伸到多远。

senses.title: Size or range
senses.definition: the size, area, or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小、面积或范围
senses.example: The extent of the forest surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 森林的范围让我们惊讶。
senses.why: Degree in an abstract sense becomes physical size.
senses.whyCN: 抽象程度变成具体的大小范围。

senses.title: A limit
senses.definition: the limit beyond which something does not go
senses.definitionCN: 某事物不再超出的界限
senses.example: He went to the full extent of his power.
senses.exampleCN: 他用尽了权力的全部限度。
senses.why: The far edge of a stretch becomes a limit.
senses.whyCN: 伸展的最远端变成限度。

intro.en: Extent comes from Old French estente, from Latin extendere, to stretch out.
intro.cn: extent 来自古法语 estente，根源是拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸）。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Estente means a stretch or reach.
items.cn: estente 意为伸展或延伸的范围。

items.en: Extent names the reach of a thing.
items.cn: extent 指事物的延伸范围。

items.en: Extent also means degree.
items.cn: extent 也表示程度。

items.en: To some extent becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: to some extent 成为常用短语。

note.en: Extent is how far; extend is the verb to stretch.
note.cn: extent 是延伸的程度，extend 则是拉伸的动词。

entries.definition: the level or amount of something
the size or level of something

normalIntro.en: Extent measures how far something reaches or how true it is.
normalIntro.cn: extent 衡量事物延伸到多远，或成立到什么程度。

normal.en: To some extent, the plan worked well.
normal.cn: 在某种程度上，这个计划很奏效。

normal.en: The extent of the damage is still unknown.
We were shocked by the extent of the poverty.
normal.cn: 贫困的程度让我们震惊。

normal.en: To a large extent, success depends on practice.
normal.cn: 成功在很大程度上取决于练习。

normal.en: He pushed the machine to its full extent.

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across an unknown distance.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子横在一段未知的距离上。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that marks how strong a feeling is.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标出情绪强弱程度的刻度尺。

abstract.en: Think of a boundary set at the far edge.
abstract.cn: 想象在远端划出的一条界限。

examples.en: The extent of the flood damage is not clear.
examples.cn: 洪水破坏的范围尚不清楚。

examples.en: To some extent, I understand your choice.
examples.cn: 在某种程度上，我理解你的选择。

examples.en: They explored the full extent of the cave.
examples.cn: 他们探索了洞穴的全部范围。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词形记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extent 与 extend 同源，动词是「延伸」，名词就是「延伸到的程度与范围」。

root: 源自古法语 estente，追溯到拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），核心义「延伸所达到的程度与范围」。

sensesIntro.en: Extent means the degree of something, its size or range, or a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: extent 意为某事的程度、其大小范围，或限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler measuring how far something reaches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把量出延伸距离的尺子。

branches.en: The base sense is the degree a quality reaches.
branches.cn: 基础义是某种性质达到的程度。

branches.en: Abstract degree becomes physical size.
branches.cn: 抽象程度变成具体大小。

branches.en: The far edge of a stretch becomes a limit.
branches.cn: 伸展的最远端变成限度。

branches.en: Degree and range both answer how far.
branches.cn: 程度与范围都在回答「有多远」。

branches.en: Size and limit mark the ends of the same measure.
branches.cn: 大小与限度标记同一把尺子的两端。

intro.en: Extent belongs to the extend family and shares the Latin root tendere.
intro.cn: extent 属于 extend 词族，共享拉丁词根 tendere。

latinIntro.en: Latin extendere and tendere lie behind extent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extendere 与 tendere 是 extent 的来源。

items.example: The extent of the loss was huge.
The report compares the extents of damage.
items.exampleCN: 报告比较了各处的损坏范围。

items.example: He has a tendency to worry.

items.exampleCN: 房间里的紧张气氛加剧。

items.meaning: a shelter held by stretched cloth
items.example: They pitched a tent by the lake.

definition_en: on or from the outside; coming from another place or group; relating to foreign countries
core_image: 一股来自屋外的风推开窗户
scene: 外部压力迫使公司改变计划。External pressure forced the company to change its plan.
sceneCN: 这里 external 是「外来的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：外部压力迫使公司改变计划。

senses.title: On the outside
senses.definition: located on or forming the outside of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于外部或构成外部的
senses.example: The external walls are painted white.
senses.why: The core sense is physical position outside.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是位于外部的物理位置。

senses.title: Coming from outside
senses.definition: coming from another place, person, or system
senses.definitionCN: 来自其他地方、人或系统的
senses.example: External pressure changed the decision.
senses.why: Position becomes the source of influence.
senses.whyCN: 位置变成影响的来源。

senses.title: Relating to foreign affairs
senses.definition: relating to relations with other countries
senses.definitionCN: 与别国关系有关的
senses.example: He works in external affairs.
senses.why: The outside of a country is the foreign world.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家的「外部」就是外国世界。

intro.en: External comes from Latin externus, from exterus, meaning outward.
intro.cn: external 来自拉丁语 externus，根源是 exterus（向外的）。

items.en: Exterus means outward or foreign.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的或外来的。

items.en: Externus means belonging to the outside.
items.cn: externus 意为属于外部的。

items.en: The word contrasts with internus, inner.
items.cn: 这个词与表示内部的 internus 相对。

items.en: External names what lies outside a system.
items.cn: external 指位于系统之外的事物。

items.en: External covers foreign affairs and devices.
items.cn: 现代英语中 external 涵盖对外事务与外接设备。

note.en: External is outside; internal is inside.
note.cn: external 是外部的，internal 则是内部的。

entries.definition: not inside a building or group

normalIntro.en: External marks what is outside a person, system, or country.
normalIntro.cn: external 标记人或系统、国家之外的事物。

normal.en: External doors must be locked at night.
The company faced strong external pressure.
normal.cn: 公司面临强大的外部压力。

normal.en: An external drive stores extra files.
normal.cn: 外置硬盘用来存放额外文件。

normal.en: The medicine is for external use only.
External factors slowed the economy.

abstract.en: Picture wind pushing a window open from outside.
abstract.cn: 想象风从外面把窗户吹开。

abstract.en: Imagine a voice entering a quiet room through the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音从门缝进入安静的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a country looking outward across its border.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家越过边界向外看。

examples.en: External pressure forced the manager to resign.
examples.cn: 外部压力迫使经理辞职。

examples.en: The external surface is rough and cold.
examples.cn: 外表面粗糙而冰冷。

examples.en: The country changed its external policy.
examples.cn: 这个国家改变了对外政策。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词根记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extern 表示「外部」，加形容词后缀 -al，就是 external（外部的）。

root: 源自拉丁语 externus（外部的），由 exterus（向外的）派生，核心义「位于或来自外部」。

sensesIntro.en: External means on the outside, coming from outside, or relating to foreign affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: external 意为位于外部、来自外部，或与对外事务有关。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind entering from outside a room.
core.cn: 核心意象：从屋外进入房间的风。

branches.en: The base sense is physical position outside.
branches.cn: 基础义是外部的物理位置。

branches.en: Position becomes the source of influence.
branches.cn: 位置变成影响的来源。

branches.en: The outside of a country is the foreign world.
branches.cn: 国家的「外部」就是外国世界。

branches.en: Outer walls and outside pressure share the same boundary.
branches.cn: 外墙与外部压力共享同一条边界。

branches.en: Outside forces and foreign affairs both cross a border.
branches.cn: 外部力量与对外事务都越过边界。

intro.en: External is exterus plus -al, and it belongs with exterior and extreme.
intro.cn: external 由 exterus 加 -al 构成，与 exterior、extreme 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin externus, exterus, and the suffix -alis are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 externus、exterus 与词尾 -alis 是来源要素。

items.example: She externalized her feelings in a letter.
items.exampleCN: 她在信里把感情表达出来。
污染是典型的外部性问题。

items.example: The exterior is made of brick.
Internal doors are made of wood.

definition_zh: 额外的；额外地；额外的东西
definition_en: more than usual or needed; in addition; something added or charged in addition
core_image: 账单末尾又多出来的一行小字，写着额外费用
scene: 住店要另收额外费用。The hotel charges an extra fee.
sceneCN: 这里 extra 是「额外的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：住店要另收额外费用。

senses.title: More than usual
senses.definition: more than what is usual, expected, or needed
senses.definitionCN: 多于平常、预期或所需的
senses.example: We need an extra chair for the guest.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要为客人多加一把椅子。
senses.why: The core sense is something added beyond the norm.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是超出常规而增加的东西。

senses.title: In addition
senses.definition: in addition to what is already there
senses.definitionCN: 在已有事物之外再加
senses.example: You have to pay extra for breakfast.
senses.why: The adjective becomes an adverb of addition.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为表示「额外增加」的副词。

senses.title: Something added
senses.definition: an additional item or charge
senses.definitionCN: 额外增加的项目或费用
senses.example: The room is small but the extras are free.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大，但附加项目免费。
senses.why: The quality becomes a countable thing.
senses.whyCN: 性质变成可数的具体事物。

intro.en: Extra comes from Latin extra, outside, and later shortens extraordinary.
intro.cn: extra 来自拉丁语 extra（在外面），后来也用作 extraordinary 的缩写。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面或超出。

items.en: The word appears in phrases of addition.
items.cn: 这个词出现在表示附加的短语中。

items.en: Extra becomes a short form of extraordinary.
items.cn: 英语中 extra 成为 extraordinary 的缩略形式。

items.en: Extra comes to mean additional.
items.cn: extra 逐渐表示「额外的」。

items.en: Extra covers charges, items, and effort.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extra 涵盖费用、物品与额外努力。

note.en: Extra means additional; extreme means farthest.
note.cn: extra 是额外的，extreme 则是极端的。

normalIntro.en: Extra marks anything added beyond the usual amount.
normalIntro.cn: extra 标记超出平常数量而增加的任何东西。

normal.en: We stayed an extra night in the city.
normal.cn: 我们在城里多住了一晚。

normal.en: The airline charges extra for heavy bags.
normal.cn: 航空公司对超重行李额外收费。

normal.en: She earns extra money by teaching at night.
The team practiced extra before the final.
The meal comes with extra bread.
normal.cn: 这顿饭附赠额外的面包。

abstract.en: Picture one more box added to a full shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象在满架上又加了一只箱子。

abstract.en: Imagine a bill with one small added line.
abstract.cn: 想象账单末尾多出一行小字。

abstract.en: Think of a clock with one bonus hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一天多出一个小时。

examples.en: The hotel charges extra for parking.
examples.cn: 酒店对停车额外收费。

examples.en: Take an extra sweater in case it turns cold.
examples.cn: 多带一件毛衣，以防天气转冷。

examples.en: The price includes all extras.
examples.cn: 价格包含所有附加项目。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词形记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extra 来自拉丁语「在外面」，放到账单或计划之外，就是「额外的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 extra（在外面、超出），核心义「在常规之外另加的」。

sensesIntro.en: Extra means more than usual, in addition, or an added item or charge.
sensesIntro.cn: extra 意为超出平常的、额外地，或额外项目与费用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more item added beyond the list.
core.cn: 核心意象：清单之外又添的一项。

branches.en: The base sense is something beyond the usual.
branches.cn: 基础义是超出平常的事物。

branches.en: The adjective becomes an adverb of addition.
branches.cn: 形容词变成表示附加的副词。

branches.en: The quality becomes a countable item.
branches.cn: 性质变成可数的项目。

branches.en: More than usual and in addition describe the same surplus.
branches.cn: 超出平常与额外增加描述同一种盈余。

branches.en: An extra chair and an extra charge are both additions.
branches.cn: 多一把椅子与多一笔费用都是附加。

intro.en: Extra comes from Latin extra, outside, and shares a family with extraordinary and extraneous.
intro.cn: extra 来自拉丁语 extra（在外面），与 extraordinary、extraneous 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra meaning outside is the source form.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「在外面」的拉丁语 extra 是来源形式。

items.example: The car comes with several extras.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车配有若干附加项目。

items.meaning: coming from outside and not needed

items.exampleCN: extra- 出现在 extraordinary 中。

items.meaning: a person who turns outward to others
items.exampleCN: 这个外向的人很快交了朋友。

latinEntries.example: Exterus belongs to the same family.

latinEntries.exampleCN: extraordinary 由 extra 与 ordinary 组合。

definition_en: very unusual and impressive; much greater than usual; strange and surprising
core_image: 一朵普通花丛中突然开出的巨大奇异花朵
scene: 她展现出非凡的勇气。She showed extraordinary courage.
sceneCN: 这里 extraordinary 是「非凡的、出色的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她展现出非凡的勇气。

senses.title: Far beyond usual
senses.definition: much greater or better than usual
senses.definitionCN: 远超过平常水平或质量的
senses.example: She showed extraordinary courage.
senses.why: The core sense is standing outside the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是站在平常之外。

senses.title: Very unusual
senses.definition: very unusual and not happening often
senses.definitionCN: 非常不寻常且不常发生的
senses.example: The team met under extraordinary circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在特殊情况下开会。
senses.why: Rare events stand outside normal rules.
senses.whyCN: 罕见事件站在常规之外。

senses.title: Strange and surprising
senses.definition: so strange that it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪到令人惊讶的
senses.example: He told an extraordinary story about the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个关于大海的离奇故事。
senses.why: The unusual becomes the astonishing.
senses.whyCN: 不寻常变成令人惊异。

intro.en: Extraordinary joins Latin extra, outside, and ordinarius, ordinary.
intro.cn: extraordinary 由拉丁语 extra（在外面）与 ordinarius（普通的）组合而成。

items.en: Extra means outside or beyond.
items.cn: extra 意为在外面或超出。

items.en: Ordinarius means ordinary or usual.
items.cn: ordinarius 意为普通的、通常的。

items.en: The pieces mean outside the ordinary.
items.cn: 两部分合起来意为「超出普通」。

items.en: The word passes through French into English.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extraordinary covers greatness and strangeness.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extraordinary 涵盖卓越与离奇。

note.en: Extraordinary is beyond ordinary; ordinary is usual.
note.cn: extraordinary 是超出普通的，ordinary 则是平常的。

normalIntro.en: Extraordinary describes what stands far outside the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: extraordinary 描述远远站在普通之外的事物。

normal.en: She has an extraordinary memory for names.
normal.cn: 她对名字有非凡的记忆力。

normal.en: The rescue was an extraordinary effort.
normal.cn: 这次救援是非凡的努力。

normal.en: They met under extraordinary circumstances.
normal.cn: 他们在特殊情况下会面。

normal.en: The painting is quite extraordinary.
He told an extraordinary tale of survival.
normal.cn: 他讲了一个离奇的生存故事。

abstract.en: Picture one huge flower rising above a plain field.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵巨大的花从普通田野中升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet town where something amazing happens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个安静小镇上发生了惊人的事。

abstract.en: Think of a person who does what no one thought possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人做到了大家认为不可能的事。

examples.en: The doctor made an extraordinary effort to save him.
examples.cn: 医生为救他付出了非凡的努力。

examples.en: It was an extraordinary coincidence.
examples.cn: 这是一个离奇的巧合。

examples.en: The team showed extraordinary skill.
examples.cn: 这支队伍展现了非凡的技巧。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extra（超出）加 ordinary（普通）：超出普通的，就是 extraordinary（非凡的）。

root: 由拉丁语 extra（超出）与 ordinarius（普通）组合而来，核心义「超出普通、非同寻常」。

sensesIntro.en: Extraordinary means far beyond usual, very unusual, or strange and surprising.
sensesIntro.cn: extraordinary 意为远超平常、非常不寻常，或离奇惊人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one huge flower above a plain field.
core.cn: 核心意象：普通田野上高出一切的一朵巨花。

branches.en: The base sense is greatness beyond the usual.
branches.cn: 基础义是超出平常的卓越。

branches.en: Rare events stand outside normal rules.
branches.cn: 罕见事件站在常规之外。

branches.en: The unusual becomes astonishing.
branches.cn: 不寻常变成令人惊异。

branches.en: Great ability and rare events both exceed the norm.
branches.cn: 卓越能力与罕见事件都超出常规。

branches.en: Special circumstances often produce strange stories.
branches.cn: 特殊情况常常产生离奇故事。

intro.en: Extraordinary is a compound of extra and ordinary, with a large family of related words.
intro.cn: extraordinary 是 extra 与 ordinary 的复合词，拥有一个较大的相关词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extra and ordinarius are the two source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extra 与 ordinarius 是两个来源要素。

items.example: The extraordinariness of the event shocked us.
items.exampleCN: 这件事的离奇让我们震惊。

items.example: Ordinarily, the shop closes at six.

latinEntries.exampleCN: ordo 是 ordinarius 的词源。

definition_en: very great in degree; far from what is usual or moderate; the furthest point
core_image: 温度计的水银柱冲到最顶端
scene: 该地区正经历极端天气。The region is experiencing extreme weather.
sceneCN: 这里 extreme 是「极度的、极端的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：该地区正经历极端天气。

senses.title: Very great in degree
senses.definition: very great in degree or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 程度或强度非常大的
senses.example: The desert reaches extreme temperatures.
senses.why: The core sense is the farthest point of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是刻度上最远的一点。

senses.title: Far from moderate
senses.definition: far from what is usual, moderate, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 远离通常、温和或可接受范围的
senses.example: The group holds extreme views.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体持有极端观点。
senses.why: The far end of a scale becomes a political judgment.
senses.whyCN: 刻度的远端变成政治判断。

senses.title: The furthest point
senses.definition: the furthest or most severe point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最远或最严重的点
senses.example: The two extremes rarely meet.
senses.why: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成端点本身。

intro.en: Extreme comes from Latin extremus, the superlative of exterus, outward.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 extremus，是 exterus（向外的）的最高级。

items.en: Exterus means outward.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的。

items.en: Extremus means farthest out.
items.cn: extremus 意为最靠外的。

items.en: Extreme passes through French into English.
items.cn: extreme 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Extreme describes the far end of a scale.
items.cn: extreme 描述刻度的最远端。

items.en: Extreme also describes severe weather and views.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extreme 也形容极端天气与观点。

note.en: Extreme is the far end; extra is an addition.
note.cn: extreme 是最远端，extra 则是额外添加。

entries.definition: to pass waste out of the body

normalIntro.en: Extreme points to the farthest end of any scale.
normalIntro.cn: extreme 指向任何刻度的最远端。

normal.en: The region suffers extreme heat in summer.
normal.cn: 这个地区夏天酷热难耐。

normal.en: They took extreme measures to stop the fire.
normal.cn: 他们采取极端措施阻止大火。

normal.en: The family lives in extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 这家人生活在极度贫困中。

normal.en: Do not go to extremes in dieting.
At the other extreme, the lake is frozen.
normal.cn: 在另一个极端，湖面结着冰。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer pushed to its highest mark.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计的水银冲到最高点。

abstract.en: Imagine a road ending at a cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路终止在悬崖边。

abstract.en: Think of a scale with weights at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端都压着砝码。

examples.en: The mountain is dangerous in extreme weather.
examples.cn: 在极端天气下，这座山很危险。

examples.en: Their views are too extreme for most voters.
examples.cn: 他们的观点对多数选民来说太极端。

examples.en: The temperature swung from one extreme to the other.
examples.cn: 温度从一个极端摆到另一个极端。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词根记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extreme 与 extra 同源：extra 是「超出」，extreme 是「超出到最远端」，即极端。

root: 源自拉丁语 extremus（最靠外的），是 exterus（向外的）的最高级，核心义「刻度或范围的最远端」。

sensesIntro.en: Extreme means very great in degree, far from moderate, or the furthest point.
sensesIntro.cn: extreme 意为程度极大、远离温和，或最远的端点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gauge needle at the red end.
core.cn: 核心意象：仪表指针停在红色末端。

branches.en: The base sense is the far end of a scale.
branches.cn: 基础义是刻度的最远端。

branches.en: The far end becomes a judgment of views.
branches.cn: 最远端变成对观点的评判。

branches.en: The adjective becomes the endpoint itself.
branches.cn: 形容词变成端点本身。

branches.en: Great degree and immoderate views both sit at the edge.
branches.cn: 极大程度与偏激观点都位于边缘。

branches.en: Extreme views and extreme situations share the same edge.
branches.cn: 极端观点与极端处境共享同一条边缘。

intro.en: Extreme comes from the Latin exterus family and has a large modern word family.
intro.cn: extreme 来自拉丁语 exterus 词族，现代词族很大。

latinIntro.en: Latin extremus and exterus are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extremus 与 exterus 是来源形式。

items.meaning: the furthest end or a severe situation
items.example: The injury affected the lower extremity.

items.exampleCN: 政府反对暴力极端主义。

items.example: The group was led by an extremist.
items.exampleCN: 这个团体由一名极端分子领导。

items.meaning: the opposite ends of a range
items.exampleCN: 气候在两个极端之间摆动。
极限运动吸引勇敢的人。

latinEntries.example: Extra is related to the same family.

definition_en: to a very great degree; very; in an extreme way
core_image: 仪表指针一直冲到刻度尽头
scene: 这道题极其困难。The problem is extremely difficult.
sceneCN: 这里 extremely 是「极其、非常」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这道题极其困难。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a very great degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到非常大的程度
senses.example: The water is extremely cold.
senses.why: The core sense is reaching the far end of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是达到刻度的最远端。

senses.title: At the limit
senses.definition: at the furthest limit of what is possible
senses.definitionCN: 达到可能范围的极限
senses.example: The machine is extremely sensitive.
senses.why: A high degree becomes a point near the limit.
senses.whyCN: 高程度变成接近极限的点。

senses.title: In an extreme way
senses.definition: in a way that goes far beyond what is moderate
senses.definitionCN: 以远远超出温和范围的方式
senses.example: He reacted extremely to the criticism.
senses.why: Manner joins degree at the edge of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 方式与程度在刻度边缘结合。

intro.en: Extremely is extreme plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: extremely 由 extreme 加副词词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: Extremus means farthest out.
items.cn: extremus 意为最靠外的。

items.en: The Latin form marks the highest degree.
items.cn: 拉丁语形式标记最高程度。

items.en: Extreme describes the far end.
items.cn: extreme 描述最远端。

items.en: The ending -ly turns it into a way or degree.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成方式或程度副词。

items.en: Extremely is a common intensifier.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extremely 是常用强调词。

note.en: Extremely means very; externally means from outside.
note.cn: extremely 是极其，externally 则是从外部。

normalIntro.en: Extremely pushes an adjective or adverb to the far end.
normalIntro.cn: extremely 把形容词或副词推到最远端。

normal.en: The exam was extremely difficult.
This species is extremely rare.
She was extremely pleased with the result.
The road is extremely narrow here.
He spoke extremely quietly.

abstract.en: Picture a needle pressed against the final mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针被压到最后一个刻度。

abstract.en: Imagine a volume knob turned all the way up.
abstract.cn: 想象音量旋钮被拧到最大。

abstract.en: Think of a rope pulled to its tightest.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子被拉到最紧。

examples.en: The instructions are extremely clear.
examples.cn: 说明极其清楚。

examples.en: It is extremely unlikely that he will come.
examples.cn: 他来的可能性极小。

examples.en: She was extremely careful with the glass.
examples.cn: 她对那只玻璃杯非常小心。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: extreme 加副词后缀 -ly，表示「达到极端程度」，就是 extremely。

root: 由 extreme 加 -ly 构成，根源是拉丁语 extremus（最靠外的），核心义「达到极端的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Extremely means to a very great degree, at the limit, or in an extreme way.
sensesIntro.cn: extremely 意为程度极高、达到极限，或以极端方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle at the final mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在最后刻度上的指针。

branches.en: The base sense is a very high degree.
branches.cn: 基础义是极高的程度。

branches.en: High degree becomes a point near the limit.
branches.cn: 高程度变成接近极限的点。

branches.en: Manner joins degree at the edge of a scale.
branches.cn: 方式与程度在刻度边缘结合。

branches.en: Very great and near the limit describe the same intensity.
branches.cn: 极大与接近极限描述同一种强度。

branches.en: Degree and manner can both be extreme.
branches.cn: 程度与方式都可能是极端的。

intro.en: Extremely is extreme plus -ly, and it belongs to the Latin exterus family.
intro.cn: extremely 由 extreme 加 -ly 构成，属于拉丁语 exterus 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extremus and exterus lie behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extremus 与 exterus 是该词的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这名极端分子拒绝一切妥协。

latinEntries.example: Extra belongs to the same family.

definition_en: the organ used for seeing; the ability to judge; a small hole or loop; to look at carefully
core_image: 一双明亮的眼睛，中间的瞳孔像深色的圆孔
scene: 她眼里含着泪水。There were tears in her eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 eye 是「眼睛」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她眼里含着泪水。

senses.title: The seeing organ
senses.definition: one of the two organs in the face used for seeing
senses.definitionCN: 脸上用于观看的两个器官之一
senses.example: She has bright blue eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一双明亮的蓝眼睛。
senses.why: The core sense is the body part for sight.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是用于观看的身体器官。

senses.title: A good judgment
senses.definition: the ability to notice or judge things well
senses.definitionCN: 善于察觉或判断事物的能力
senses.example: He has an eye for detail.
senses.why: Seeing becomes the power to judge.
senses.whyCN: 看见变成判断的能力。

senses.title: A small hole
senses.definition: a small hole or loop shaped like an eye
senses.definitionCN: 形状像眼睛的小孔或环
senses.example: Thread the needle through its eye.
senses.why: The shape of the organ names similar objects.
senses.whyCN: 器官的形状被用来命名相似之物。

senses.title: To look at
senses.definition: to look at something carefully or with interest
senses.definitionCN: 仔细或饶有兴趣地看某物
senses.example: He eyed the cake hungrily.
senses.exampleCN: 他饥肠辘辘地盯着蛋糕。
senses.why: The organ of sight becomes the act of watching.
senses.whyCN: 观看的器官变成注视的动作。

intro.en: Eye comes from Old English ēage, from a Germanic root linked to seeing.
intro.cn: eye 源自古英语 ēage，来自与「看」有关的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Eage names the organ of sight.
items.cn: eage 指观看的器官。

items.en: The root is linked to the act of seeing.
items.cn: 这个词根与「看」的动作有关。

items.en: Eage combines with other words for eyelids and brows.
items.cn: eage 与其他词组合成眼皮与眉毛等词。

items.en: Eye keeps the body sense and gains figurative uses.
items.cn: 中古英语中 eye 保留身体义并获得引申义。

items.en: Eye also means judgment and a small hole.
items.cn: 现代英语中 eye 也指眼光与小孔。

note.en: Eye is the organ; ewe is a female sheep.
note.cn: eye 是眼睛，ewe 则是母羊，两者读音相同。

entries.definition: having eyes of a stated kind
the ability to see or plan

normalIntro.en: Eye is the organ of sight and also the act of watching.
normalIntro.cn: eye 是观看的器官，也可指注视的动作。

normal.en: She closed her eyes and listened.
Keep an eye on the children.
The bright sign caught my eye.
normal.cn: 明亮的招牌吸引了我的注意。

normal.en: He has a good eye for color.
The needle's eye is very small.

abstract.en: Picture two round windows looking onto the world.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇圆形的小窗望向世界。

abstract.en: Imagine a camera lens opening and closing.
abstract.cn: 想象相机镜头张开又合上。

abstract.en: Think of a pupil widening in dim light.
abstract.cn: 想象瞳孔在暗光中放大。

examples.en: He looked me straight in the eye.
examples.cn: 他直视我的眼睛。

examples.en: She has an eye for old furniture.
examples.cn: 她对旧家具有眼光。

examples.en: The cat eyed the bird from the window.
examples.cn: 猫从窗内盯着那只鸟。

dict_mnemonic.note: 字形记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: eye 的两个 e 像两只眼睛，中间的 y 像鼻子，一眼就记住「眼睛」。

root: 源自古英语 ēage，来自日耳曼语中与「看」有关的词根，核心义「观看的器官」及其引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eye means the organ of sight, good judgment, an eye-shaped hole, or to look at something.
sensesIntro.cn: eye 意为观看的器官、眼光、眼状小孔，或注视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright pupil inside a round eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：圆眼睛里明亮的瞳孔。

branches.en: The base sense is the organ of sight.
branches.cn: 基础义是观看的器官。

branches.en: Seeing becomes the power to judge.
branches.cn: 看见变成判断的能力。

branches.en: The shape names similar small objects.
branches.cn: 形状被用来命名相似的小物件。

branches.en: The organ becomes the act of watching.
branches.cn: 器官变成注视的动作。

branches.en: The eye and the act of using it are closely linked.
branches.cn: 眼睛与使用眼睛的动作紧密相连。

intro.en: Eye is a native English word that forms many compounds, from eyelid to eyesight.
intro.cn: eye 是英语本族词，构成从 eyelid 到 eyesight 的许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Eye has no Latin root; it comes from Old English eage.
latinIntro.cn: eye 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 eage。

items.meaning: organ of sight or to watch

items.exampleCN: 好视力在夜间很有帮助。

items.example: The empty building is an eyesore.

definition_en: the front of the head; the front surface of something; to turn toward something; to deal with a difficulty
core_image: 一张正对镜头的脸，背后是必须直面的墙
scene: 她面对困难从不退缩。She never backs away when she faces difficulty.
sceneCN: 这里 face 是「面对、面临」（第 3 个义项）；句意：她面对困难从不退缩。

senses.title: The front of the head
senses.definition: the front part of the head where the eyes, nose, and mouth are
senses.definitionCN: 头部前面长有眼睛、鼻子和嘴的部位
senses.example: She washed her face with cold water.
senses.why: The core sense is the front of the head.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是头部的前面。

senses.title: The front surface
senses.definition: the front or outer surface of an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体的前面或外表面
senses.example: The face of the clock is cracked.
senses.why: The front of the head names the front of things.
senses.whyCN: 头部的前面被用来命名物体的正面。

senses.title: Turn toward
senses.definition: to turn or point toward someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 转向或朝向某人某物
senses.example: The house faces the sea.
senses.why: The front becomes the direction one turns.
senses.whyCN: 正面变成所朝的方向。

senses.title: Deal with difficulty
senses.definition: to have to deal with a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 不得不应对困难处境
senses.example: The company faces rising costs.
senses.why: Facing a person becomes facing a problem.
senses.whyCN: 面对一个人变成面对一个问题。

intro.en: Face comes from Latin facies, form or appearance, through Old French face.
intro.cn: face 经古法语 face 来自拉丁语 facies，意为形状或外观。

items.en: Facies means form, shape, or appearance.
items.cn: facies 意为形状、外形或外观。

items.en: The word covers both a face and a surface.
items.cn: 这个词兼指面孔与表面。

items.en: Face keeps the sense of front and look.
items.cn: 古法语 face 保留「正面与外观」之义。

items.en: Face becomes the common word for the front of the head.
items.cn: 中古英语中 face 成为表示面孔的常用词。

items.en: Face also means to confront a problem.
items.cn: 现代英语中 face 也指面对问题。

note.en: Face is the front; fact is something true.
note.cn: face 是正面，fact 则是事实。

normalIntro.en: Face moves from the front of the head to the front of things and to facing trouble.
normalIntro.cn: face 从头部正面扩展到物体正面，再到面对困难。

normal.en: She has a kind face.
The north face of the mountain is cold.
We sat face to face across the table.
normal.cn: 我们隔着桌子面对面坐着。

normal.en: The team faces a serious problem.
normal.cn: 团队面临一个严重问题。

normal.en: He made a face at the bitter medicine.
normal.cn: 他对着苦药做了个鬼脸。

abstract.en: Picture a face looking straight into a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象一张正对镜子的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine a wall that stands against the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一面迎着风的墙。

abstract.en: Think of a person stepping toward a hard task.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人迈向艰难任务。

examples.en: The building faces the main square.
examples.cn: 这栋建筑面向主广场。

examples.en: We must face the facts honestly.
examples.cn: 我们必须诚实面对事实。

examples.en: Her face showed no fear.
examples.cn: 她脸上没有露出恐惧。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: face 谐音「费事」：遇到麻烦要 face（面对），确实费事。

root: 源自拉丁语 facies（形状、外观），经古法语 face 进入英语，核心义「正面、面孔」及「正面对待」。

sensesIntro.en: Face means the front of the head, the front surface, to turn toward, or to deal with difficulty.
sensesIntro.cn: face 意为头部正面、物体表面、朝向，或面对困难。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face turned straight toward the viewer.
core.cn: 核心意象：正对观看者的一张脸。

branches.en: The base sense is the front of the head.
branches.cn: 基础义是头部的前面。

branches.en: The head's front names the front of objects.
branches.cn: 头部正面被用来命名物体正面。

branches.en: The front becomes the direction one turns.
branches.cn: 正面变成所朝的方向。

branches.en: Facing a person becomes facing a problem.
branches.cn: 面对一个人变成面对一个问题。

branches.en: Turning toward a thing and confronting it share one motion.
branches.cn: 朝向某物与直面某物共享同一动作。

intro.en: Face comes from Latin facies and builds facial, facing, and faceless.
intro.cn: face 来自拉丁语 facies，并构成 facial、facing 与 faceless。

latinIntro.en: Latin facies and facere are related source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facies 与 facere 是相关的来源形式。

items.meaning: front of the head or to confront
more than one face or confronts
items.meaningCN: 面孔（复数）；面对（第三人称）

items.example: The room facing the sea is bright.
items.exampleCN: 面朝大海的房间很明亮。
看不清面孔的人群继续前行。
他们举行了面对面的会议。

definition_en: a place or piece of equipment built for a purpose; an ability to do something easily; the quality of being easy to do
core_image: 一个让事情做起来更省力的装置或场所
scene: 这所学校有现代化的体育设施。The school has modern sports facilities.
sceneCN: 这里 facility 是「设施、设备」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这所学校有现代化的体育设施。

senses.title: A built place or equipment
senses.definition: a place, building, or piece of equipment built for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的建造的场所、建筑或设备
senses.example: The hotel has excellent sports facilities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店有极好的体育设施。
senses.why: The core sense is something made to make an activity possible.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是为使某项活动成为可能而建造的东西。

senses.title: An easy ability
senses.definition: a natural or learned ability to do something easily
senses.definitionCN: 轻松做某事的天生或习得能力
senses.example: She has a facility for learning languages.
senses.why: The made thing becomes a mental tool that makes action easy.
senses.whyCN: 人造之物变成使行动轻松的心智工具。

senses.title: Ease in doing
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to do or use
senses.definitionCN: 容易做或容易使用的性质
senses.example: He answered the questions with facility.
senses.why: The idea of ease is the abstract side of the same root.
senses.whyCN: 「容易」是同一词根的抽象一面。

intro.en: Facility comes from Latin facilitas, ease, from facilis, easy.
intro.cn: facility 来自拉丁语 facilitas（容易），源头是 facilis（容易的）。

items.en: Facilis means easy to do.
items.cn: facilis 意为容易做的。

items.en: Facilitas means ease or readiness.
items.cn: facilitas 意为容易或敏捷。

items.en: Facilite carries the sense of ease.
items.cn: facilite 带有轻松之义。

items.en: Facility comes to name buildings and equipment.
items.cn: 现代英语中 facility 转而指建筑与设备。

items.en: Facilities usually means a set of services.
items.cn: 当代英语中 facilities 通常指一整套服务设施。

note.en: Facility is a place or ease; faculty is an ability or department.
note.cn: facility 是设施或便利，faculty 则是能力或院系。

entries.definition: an ability or an academic department
the things needed for an activity

normalIntro.en: Facility covers both the place that helps you and the ease you feel.
normalIntro.cn: facility 既指帮助你的设施，也指你感到的轻松。

normal.en: The campus has excellent library facilities.
normal.cn: 校园有极好的图书馆设施。

normal.en: The clinic lacks basic medical facilities.
normal.cn: 这家诊所缺乏基本医疗设施。

normal.en: She has a facility for remembering names.
The new software improves facility of use.
normal.cn: 新软件提升了使用的便利性。

normal.en: They toured the research facility.

abstract.en: Picture a smooth ramp that makes a hard climb easy.
abstract.cn: 想象一条让艰难攀爬变轻松的平滑坡道。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand that finds every task light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只把每件事都做得轻松的手。

abstract.en: Think of a well-equipped room waiting to be used.
abstract.cn: 想象一间设备齐全、随时可用的房间。

examples.en: The city built new facilities for cyclists.
examples.cn: 这座城市为骑行者建造了新设施。

examples.en: His facility with numbers impressed the team.
examples.cn: 他对数字的敏锐让团队印象深刻。

examples.en: The task was completed with surprising facility.
examples.cn: 这项任务完成得异常轻松。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: facility 与 facile、facilitate 同源于拉丁语 facilis（容易的），凡是「设施」都是为了让事情更容易。

root: facility 源自拉丁语 facilitas（容易），来自 facilis（容易的），与 facilitate、facile 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Facility is a built place or equipment, an easy ability, or the quality of ease.
sensesIntro.cn: facility 指建成的设施设备、轻松的能力，或容易的性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that makes a task easier.
core.cn: 核心意象：让任务变得更轻松的东西。

branches.en: The base sense is the built place or equipment.
branches.cn: 基础义是建成的场所或设备。

branches.en: The tool becomes a mental ability.
branches.cn: 工具引申为心智能力。

branches.en: Ease is the abstract quality behind both.
branches.cn: 容易是两者背后的抽象性质。

branches.en: Both remove difficulty from an activity.
branches.cn: 两者都消除活动的难度。

branches.en: An ability is shown by acting with ease.
branches.cn: 能力体现为轻松地行动。

intro.en: Facility belongs to the fac- family of Latin origin meaning to do or make.
intro.cn: facility 属于源自拉丁语、意为「做或制造」的 fac- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, facilis, and facilitas explain this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、facilis 与 facilitas 解释了这个词族。

items.meaning: services and equipment for a purpose

items.exampleCN: 这个应用促进了团队合作。

items.meaning: one who makes a process easier
items.example: The facilitator kept the meeting on track.
items.exampleCN: 协调人让会议保持正轨。

items.example: The sports facility has a pool.
items.exampleCN: 这个体育设施有游泳池。

latinEntries.example: Facere is the root of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语词的词根。

definition_en: a thing that is known to be true; reality as it actually is; a deed or act
core_image: 一件已经做成、无法更改的事情摆在眼前
scene: 事实上，我从未去过那里。In fact, I have never been there.
sceneCN: 这里 fact 是「事实、真相」（第 1 个义项）；句意：事实上，我从未去过那里。

derivatives.zh: 趣闻；未经证实的小信息

senses.title: A true statement
senses.definition: a piece of information that is known to be true
senses.definitionCN: 已知为真的一条信息
senses.example: It is a fact that water boils at one hundred degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 水在一百度沸腾，这是事实。
senses.why: The core sense is something done and therefore true.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是已经发生因而为真的事。

senses.title: Reality
senses.definition: reality as it actually is, especially when it differs from hope
senses.definitionCN: 实际存在的现实，尤指与期望不同时
senses.example: The fact is that we cannot afford it.
senses.why: Truth turns into the hard reality that limits us.
senses.whyCN: 真相转化为限制我们的严酷现实。

senses.title: A deed
senses.definition: an act or deed, especially in legal use
senses.definitionCN: 行为或事迹，尤用于法律语境
senses.example: The court judged the fact, not the intention.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭裁决的是行为本身，而非意图。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply something done.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「做过的事」。

intro.en: Fact comes from Latin factum, a thing done, from facere, to do.
intro.cn: fact 来自拉丁语 factum（做成的事），源头 facere（做）。

items.en: Factum means a deed or event.
items.cn: factum 意为行为或事件。

items.en: Facere means to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: English fact means a deed or crime.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 fact 指行为或罪行。

items.en: Fact shifts to mean something true.
items.cn: 十七世纪 fact 转为「真实之事」。

items.en: In fact and the fact that become fixed phrases.
items.cn: in fact 与 the fact that 成为固定搭配。

note.en: A fact is true; a factor is something that influences a result.
note.cn: fact 是事实，factor 则是影响因素。

entries.definition: one side of a subject or gem

normalIntro.en: Fact is what has been done and cannot be argued away.
normalIntro.cn: fact 是已经做成、无法辩驳的事。

normal.en: The fact is that the shop is closed.
In fact, she knew the answer all along.
normal.cn: 事实上，她一直知道答案。

normal.en: As a matter of fact, I agree with you.
We need facts, not guesses.
normal.cn: 我们需要事实，而不是猜测。

normal.en: It is a fact of life that prices rise.
normal.cn: 物价上涨是生活的现实。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed onto paper: it is done.
abstract.cn: 想象印章压在纸上：事情已成定局。

abstract.en: Imagine a stone that cannot be argued with.
abstract.cn: 想象一块无法争辩的石头。

abstract.en: Think of a deed recorded in a court book.
abstract.cn: 想象记在法庭卷宗里的行为。

examples.en: The report is based on facts.
examples.cn: 这份报告以事实为依据。

examples.en: It is a fact that she works harder than anyone.
examples.cn: 她比任何人都努力，这是事实。

examples.en: The fact that he apologized changed nothing.
examples.cn: 他道歉这一事实并没有改变什么。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: fact 来自拉丁语 factum（做成的事），同族词有 factory、factor、facility，记住「做了就成为事实」。

root: fact 源自拉丁语 factum（已成之事），来自 facere（做），与 factory、factor、facility 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Fact is a true piece of information, hard reality, or a deed.
sensesIntro.cn: fact 指真实的资讯、严酷的现实，或行为事迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deed already done and fixed in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：已经做成、固定下来的事。

branches.en: The base sense is a true piece of information.
branches.cn: 基础义是真实的资讯。

branches.en: Truth becomes the hard reality that limits us.
branches.cn: 真相变成限制我们的严酷现实。

branches.en: The oldest sense is simply a deed done.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项就是做过的行为。

branches.en: Facts describe reality as it is.
branches.cn: 事实描述现实的本来面目。

branches.en: A deed is a fact that someone caused.
branches.cn: 行为是由人造成的事实。

intro.en: Fact is the noun form of the Latin root fac- meaning to do or make.
intro.cn: fact 是拉丁词根 fac-（做、制造）的名词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere and factum underlie fact and its compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 与 factum 构成 fact 及其复合词的基础。

items.exampleCN: 这篇文章以事实为依据。
这份报告在事实上正确。
他们派出了实情调查小组。

items.example: As a matter of fact, I was there.

latinEntries.example: Facere is the root of fact.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 是 fact 的词根。

definition_en: one of the things that influences a result; a number that divides another exactly or is multiplied with others; a substance that takes part in a process
core_image: 几股力量共同推动一个结果，其中一股就是 factor
scene: 价格是影响选择的关键因素。Price is a key factor in the choice.
sceneCN: 这里 factor 是「因素、要素」（第 1 个义项）；句意：价格是影响选择的关键因素。

senses.title: An influence on a result
senses.definition: one of the things that influences a result
senses.definitionCN: 影响结果的事物之一
senses.example: Cost was the main factor in our decision.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是我们决定的主要因素。
senses.why: The core sense is a maker of an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是结果的促成者。

senses.title: A mathematical multiplier
senses.definition: a number that is multiplied with another or divides another exactly
senses.definitionCN: 与另一数相乘或能整除另一数的数
senses.example: Three and four are factors of twelve.
senses.why: A number that helps build a product is a maker in arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 帮助构成乘积的数在算术中也是「制造者」。

senses.title: A biological substance
senses.definition: a substance that takes part in a body process
senses.definitionCN: 参与身体某种过程的物质
senses.example: The doctor tested for a clotting factor.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检测了一种凝血因子。
senses.why: An active substance is treated as an agent in a process.
senses.whyCN: 起作用的物质被视为过程的动因。

intro.en: Factor comes from Latin factor, a doer, from facere, to do.
intro.cn: factor 来自拉丁语 factor（做事者），源头 facere（做）。

items.en: Factor means a maker or doer.
items.cn: factor 意为制造者或行动者。

items.en: Facere means to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: Factor names a business agent.
items.cn: 十五世纪 factor 指商业代理人。

items.en: The word comes to mean a multiplier.
items.cn: 数学中该词转为因数。

items.en: Factor means any influence on a result.
items.cn: 现代英语中 factor 指影响结果的任何因素。

note.en: A factor influences a result; a factory makes goods.
note.cn: factor 影响结果，factory 则制造产品。

entries.definition: a building where goods are made
something that makes a result happen
one part of a larger system

normalIntro.en: A factor is one of the forces that makes a result happen.
normalIntro.cn: factor 是促成结果的诸般力量之一。

normal.en: Weather was a factor in the delay.
normal.cn: 天气是延误的一个因素。

normal.en: Diet is a risk factor for heart disease.
normal.cn: 饮食是心脏病的风险因素。

normal.en: We must factor in the cost of travel.
normal.cn: 我们必须把旅费考虑在内。

normal.en: Two is a factor of eight.
Labour is a factor of production.

abstract.en: Picture several hands pushing one ball.
abstract.cn: 想象好几只手推同一个球。

abstract.en: Imagine numbers stacked to form a product.
abstract.cn: 想象几个数字叠成一个乘积。

abstract.en: Think of a chemical messenger switching a process on.
abstract.cn: 想象一种化学信使启动某个过程。

examples.en: Several factors led to the company's success.
examples.cn: 有几个因素促成了这家公司的成功。

examples.en: The teacher factored effort into the grade.
examples.cn: 老师把努力程度计入了成绩。

examples.en: Five is a prime factor of twenty.
examples.cn: 五是二十的一个质因数。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: factor 原指「做事的人」，来自 facere（做）；能左右结果的那股力量，也就成了「因素」。

root: factor 源自拉丁语 factor（做事者、制造者），来自 facere（做），由「行动者」引申为影响结果的「因素」。

sensesIntro.en: Factor is an influence on a result, a multiplying number, or an active body substance.
sensesIntro.cn: factor 指影响结果的因素、相乘的因数，或体内起作用的因子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one of several forces shaping a result.
core.cn: 核心意象：塑造结果的诸股力量之一。

branches.en: The base sense is an influence on an outcome.
branches.cn: 基础义是影响结果的因素。

branches.en: Arithmetic treats a multiplier as a maker.
branches.cn: 算术把乘数视为「制造者」。

branches.en: Medicine treats an active substance as an agent.
branches.cn: 医学把活性物质视为动因。

branches.en: Both senses involve building a larger result.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及构成更大的结果。

branches.en: Physical and abstract forces can both be factors.
branches.cn: 具体与抽象的力量都可能是因素。

intro.en: Factor is built from the Latin root fact- plus the agent ending -or.
intro.cn: factor 由拉丁词根 fact- 加施动后缀 -or 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin factor and facere explain factor and its mathematical relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 factor 与 facere 解释了 factor 及其数学同族词。

items.example: Tax was factored into the price.
Factoring in inflation changes the figure.

items.exampleCN: 把这个表达式因式分解。

items.meaning: a product of all positive integers up to a number
items.example: Five factorial equals one hundred twenty.
items.exampleCN: 五的阶乘等于一百二十。

items.meaning: an input such as labour or land
items.example: Capital is a factor of production.

latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 提供 fact- 词干。

latinEntries.example: Factus explains the stem in compound words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: factus 解释了复合词中的词干。

definition_zh: 工厂；制造厂；大量生产某种事物的地方
definition_en: a building or group of buildings where goods are made; a historic trading post abroad; a place that produces something in large quantities
core_image: 厂房里机器轰鸣，流水线不断吐出产品
scene: 这家工厂每天生产上千辆自行车。The factory produces a thousand bicycles a day.
sceneCN: 这里 factory 是「工厂、制造厂」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家工厂每天生产上千辆自行车。

senses.title: A manufacturing plant
senses.definition: a building or group of buildings where goods are made
senses.definitionCN: 制造商品的建筑或建筑群
senses.example: The factory makes parts for cars.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产汽车零件。
senses.why: The core sense is a place where making happens.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是进行制造的场所。

senses.title: A historic trading post
senses.definition: a trading station set up by merchants in another country
senses.definitionCN: 商人在他国设立的贸易据点
senses.example: The old factory traded spices and cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧商站经营香料和布匹。
senses.why: A factor governed trade there, so the place took the name.
senses.whyCN: 代理人在那里管理贸易，因此该地得名。

senses.title: A place of mass production
senses.definition: a place that produces a particular thing in large quantities
senses.definitionCN: 大量生产某种特定事物的地方
senses.example: The city is a factory of new ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是新思想的生产地。
senses.why: The image of mass production extends to abstract output.
senses.whyCN: 大批量生产的意象延伸到抽象产出。

intro.en: Factory comes from factor, a business agent, with the place ending -y.
intro.cn: factory 由 factor（商业代理人）加表示场所的后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Factor means a doer or agent.
items.cn: factor 意为做事者或代理人。

items.en: Factor names a merchant's deputy.
items.cn: 十五世纪 factor 指商人的代理人。

items.en: Factory names a trading post abroad.
items.cn: 十六世纪 factory 指海外贸易站。

items.en: The word shifts to a building for manufacture.
items.cn: 工业时代该词转为制造厂房。

items.en: Factory means any large-scale maker.
items.cn: 现代英语中 factory 泛指大规模生产场所。

note.en: A factory is a building; a facility is a service or equipment.
note.cn: factory 是厂房，facility 则是设施或设备。

entries.definition: a place or equipment for a purpose
a building where material is processed

normalIntro.en: Factory is the place where a factor of production does its work.
normalIntro.cn: factory 就是生产要素施展身手的地方。

normal.en: He works in a shoe factory.
The factory closed last year.
Factory workers demanded better pay.
normal.cn: 工厂工人要求提高工资。

normal.en: They bought clothes at a factory outlet.
normal.cn: 他们在工厂直销店买了衣服。

normal.en: The town was a factory of skilled workers.
normal.cn: 这座镇子培养出大量熟练工人。

abstract.en: Picture rows of machines turning raw metal into parts.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排机器把金属原料变成零件。

abstract.en: Imagine a warehouse full of identical boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库里堆满一模一样的箱子。

abstract.en: Think of a place that never stops producing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个永不停歇的生产之地。

examples.en: The factory employs three hundred people.
examples.cn: 这家工厂雇用了三百人。

examples.en: Goods are shipped from the factory by rail.
examples.cn: 货物由铁路从工厂运出。

examples.en: The old factory is now a museum.
examples.cn: 这座旧工厂现在是一座博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 代理人
dict_mnemonic.text: factory 原指 factor（商业代理人）工作的地方，工业革命后才变成「制造产品的工厂」。

root: factory 由 factor（代理人、做事者）加场所后缀 -y 构成，原指代理人驻地，后演变为制造工厂。

sensesIntro.en: Factory is a manufacturing building, a historic trading post, or a place of mass production.
sensesIntro.cn: factory 指制造厂房、历史贸易站，或大量生产某物的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: machines turning raw material into finished goods.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器把原料变成成品。

branches.en: The base sense is a place of manufacture.
branches.cn: 基础义是制造场所。

branches.en: History keeps the trading-post sense.
branches.cn: 历史上的贸易站义仍保留。

branches.en: The image extends to any mass producer.
branches.cn: 该意象延伸到任何大批量生产者。

branches.en: Both senses stress large-scale output.
branches.cn: 两个义项都强调大规模产出。

branches.en: The trading post grew into the industrial plant.
branches.cn: 贸易站成长为工业厂房。

intro.en: Factory joins the agent word factor with the place suffix -y.
intro.cn: factory 由施动词 factor 加场所后缀 -y 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin factor and the medieval factoria stand behind factory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 factor 与中古拉丁语 factoria 是 factory 的前身。

items.meaning: a place where goods are made
items.example: The factory runs day and night.
New factories opened near the port.

items.meaning: a person employed in a factory
items.example: The factory worker joined a union.
items.exampleCN: 这名工厂工人加入了工会。

items.example: Safety rules apply on the factory floor.

items.meaning: a shop selling goods at reduced prices
items.example: The factory outlet sells last season's stock.
items.exampleCN: 工厂直销店出售上一季的库存。
工厂化养殖引发伦理问题。

items.meaning: produced in a factory rather than by hand
a ship that processes fish at sea
items.example: The factory ship processes the catch.
items.exampleCN: 加工船在海上处理渔获。

items.example: It was a factory town for a century.
items.exampleCN: 它做了一个世纪的工业城镇。

latinEntries.example: Factor is the base of factory.
latinEntries.exampleCN: factor 是 factory 的基础。

latinEntries.example: Factoria is the direct ancestor of factory.
latinEntries.exampleCN: factoria 是 factory 的直接前身。

definition_zh: 失败；不及格；出故障；衰退
definition_en: to be unsuccessful in doing something; to not pass an exam or test; to stop working properly; to become weaker or worse
core_image: 一根绷紧的绳子突然断掉，事情没能撑到最后
scene: 他没通过驾驶考试。He failed the driving test.
sceneCN: 这里 fail 是「不及格、未通过」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他没通过驾驶考试。

senses.title: To be unsuccessful
senses.definition: to be unsuccessful in achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 未能成功达成某事
senses.example: They tried to save the company but failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们试图挽救公司，但失败了。
senses.why: The core sense is not reaching the intended result.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是未能达到预期结果。

senses.title: To not pass a test
senses.definition: to not reach the required standard in an exam or test
senses.definitionCN: 在考试或测试中未达到规定标准
senses.example: She failed her driving test twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她两次没通过驾驶考试。
senses.why: An exam is a measured goal that can be missed.
senses.whyCN: 考试是一个可以被错过的可衡量目标。

senses.title: To stop working
senses.definition: to stop working properly
senses.definitionCN: 停止正常运转
senses.example: The brakes failed on the hill.
senses.why: A machine that cannot do its job has failed it.
senses.whyCN: 无法完成任务的机器就是「失职」了。

senses.title: To grow weaker
senses.definition: to become weaker, especially in health or energy
senses.definitionCN: 尤指健康或精力变弱
senses.example: His eyesight is failing with age.
senses.exampleCN: 随着年龄增长，他的视力在衰退。
senses.why: A body that cannot keep its strength has failed it.
senses.whyCN: 无法维持力量的身体就是「不济」了。

intro.en: Fail comes from Old French faillir, from Latin fallere, to deceive or disappoint.
intro.cn: fail 来自古法语 faillir，源头是拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、使人失望）。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive or disappoint.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使人失望。

items.en: Faillir means to be lacking or miss.
items.cn: faillir 意为欠缺或错过。

items.en: Fail means to come short of a goal.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fail 意为未达目标。

items.en: Fail also means to break down.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中 fail 也指出故障。

items.en: Fail covers exams, machines, and health.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fail 涵盖考试、机器与健康。

note.en: Fail means not succeed; fall means to drop down.
note.cn: fail 是失败，fall 则是落下。

entries.definition: to prevent a plan from succeeding

normalIntro.en: Fail covers a missed goal, a failed exam, a broken machine, and fading health.
normalIntro.cn: fail 涵盖未达目标、考试不及格、机器故障与健康衰退。

normal.en: He failed to answer the question.
She failed the entrance exam.
The engine failed during the flight.
His health began to fail.
Call me every morning without fail.
normal.cn: 每天早上务必给我打电话。

abstract.en: Picture a rope snapping just before the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子在终点线前突然断裂。

abstract.en: Imagine a red cross on an exam paper.
abstract.cn: 想象试卷上的红叉。

abstract.en: Think of a machine falling silent mid-task.
abstract.cn: 想象机器在任务中途突然安静。

examples.en: The plan failed because of poor planning.
examples.cn: 计划因规划不周而失败。

examples.en: The student failed two subjects.
examples.cn: 这名学生有两门课不及格。

examples.en: The power supply failed during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨中供电中断了。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: fail 与 false 同源于拉丁语 fallere（欺骗），「让人失望」就是 fail 的核心感觉。

root: fail 经由古法语 faillir 来自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、使人失望），与 false、fault 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Fail means not succeed, not pass, stop working, or grow weaker.
sensesIntro.cn: fail 意为失败、不及格、出故障或衰退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a support that gives way at the decisive moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：关键时刻垮掉的支撑。

branches.en: The base sense is missing the intended result.
branches.cn: 基础义是错过预期结果。

branches.en: An exam is a goal that can be missed.
branches.cn: 考试是一个可能错过的目标。

branches.en: A machine fails when it cannot work.
branches.cn: 机器无法运转就是失败。

branches.en: Health fails when strength gives way.
branches.cn: 力量垮掉时健康就衰退。

branches.en: Machine and body both stop sustaining output.
branches.cn: 机器与身体都停止维持输出。

intro.en: Fail is the verb behind failure, failing, and unfailing.
intro.cn: fail 是 failure、failing 与 unfailing 背后的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere, to deceive, is the distant source of fail and false.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗）是 fail 与 false 的远源。

items.meaning: to miss a goal or stop working
items.example: Do not be afraid to fail.

items.exampleCN: 没有支持，这个计划会失败。

items.meaning: a weakness or the act of failing
items.exampleCN: 缺乏耐心不是他的缺点。

items.example: The failure taught them a lot.
items.exampleCN: 这次失败让他们学到很多。
她给予了始终如一的支持。

items.meaning: designed to stop safely if something fails
items.example: The system has a fail-safe switch.
items.exampleCN: 该系统有一个故障安全开关。

items.meaning: an automatic switch to a backup system
items.exampleCN: 故障转移让服务保持在线。

items.example: He arrives at eight without fail.

latinEntries.example: Fallere is the root of fail.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fallere 是 fail 的词根。
fallax 是 fallacious 的前身。

definition_zh: 失败；失败的人或事；故障；未做到
definition_en: a lack of success; a person or thing that is unsuccessful; a breakdown in a machine or system; the fact of not doing something required
core_image: 一场努力最终没有抵达终点
scene: 停电使机器全部停止运转。The power failure stopped all the machines.
sceneCN: 这里 failure 是「故障」（第 3 个义项）；句意：停电使机器全部停止运转。

senses.title: A lack of success
senses.definition: a lack of success in achieving something
senses.definitionCN: 在达成某事上缺乏成功
senses.example: The project ended in failure.
senses.why: The base sense is the general state of not succeeding.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是未能成功的总体状态。

senses.title: An unsuccessful person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that is unsuccessful
senses.definitionCN: 不成功的人或事物
senses.example: The film was a complete failure.
senses.why: The abstract state becomes a countable instance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象状态变成可数的具体例子。

senses.title: A breakdown
senses.definition: a breakdown in a machine, system, or organ
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或器官的故障
senses.example: A power failure closed the airport.
senses.why: A thing that cannot work has failed its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 无法工作的东西就是未能履行职责。

senses.title: An omission
senses.definition: the fact of not doing something that is required
senses.definitionCN: 没有做被要求做的事情
senses.example: His failure to reply annoyed them.
senses.exampleCN: 他未回复让他们很恼火。
senses.why: Not doing a duty is a failure to meet it.
senses.whyCN: 未履行义务就是未能达到要求。

intro.en: Failure comes from Anglo-French failer plus the noun ending -ure.
intro.cn: failure 由盎格鲁-法语 failer 加名词后缀 -ure 构成。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive or disappoint.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使人失望。

items.en: Faillir means to miss or lack.
items.cn: faillir 意为错过或欠缺。

items.en: Failer becomes the legal verb form.
items.cn: failer 成为法律语境中的动词形式。

items.en: Failure names the state of falling short.
items.cn: 十七世纪 failure 指未达标的状况。

items.en: Failure also names machine breakdowns.
items.cn: 现代英语中 failure 也指机器故障。

note.en: Failure is the result; fail is the action.
note.cn: failure 是结果，fail 则是动作。

entries.definition: the state of losing a contest
a failure of a machine or system

normalIntro.en: Failure is the noun for every kind of fail.
normalIntro.cn: failure 是各种 fail 的名词形式。

normal.en: Failure is often the first step to success.
normal.cn: 失败常常是成功的第一步。

normal.en: The experiment was a failure.
A power failure darkened the city.
normal.cn: 一次停电让城市陷入黑暗。

normal.en: His failure to appear worried us.
normal.cn: 他没有出现让我们担心。

normal.en: The failure rate of the device is low.
normal.cn: 这个设备的故障率很低。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket falling back to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭落回地面。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge that never reaches the far bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一座始终到不了对岸的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp suddenly going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯突然熄灭。

examples.en: He learned more from failure than from success.
examples.cn: 他从失败中学到的比从成功中学到的更多。

examples.en: The engine failure forced an emergency landing.
examples.cn: 引擎故障迫使飞机紧急降落。

examples.en: Her failure to sign the form caused a delay.
examples.cn: 她未在表格上签字造成了延误。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 动词变名词
dict_mnemonic.text: fail（失败）+ -ure（名词后缀）= failure（失败），与 nature、pressure 的构词方式相同。

root: failure 由 fail（失败）加名词后缀 -ure 构成，最终源自拉丁语 fallere（使人失望）。

sensesIntro.en: Failure is lack of success, an unsuccessful thing, a breakdown, or an omission.
sensesIntro.cn: failure 指不成功、失败的人或事、故障，或未做到某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an effort that never reaches its goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：始终没有抵达目标的努力。

branches.en: The base sense is lack of success.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏成功。

branches.en: The state becomes a countable failure.
branches.cn: 状态变成可数的失败实例。

branches.en: A machine failure is a breakdown.
branches.cn: 机器 failure 就是故障。

branches.en: Failure to act is an omission.
branches.cn: 未行动就是一种疏忽。

branches.en: Broken systems and broken plans share the word.
branches.cn: 坏掉的系统与落空的计划共用一词。

intro.en: The suffix -ure turns the verb fail into a noun of result.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ure 把动词 fail 变成表示结果的名词。

latinIntro.en: Failure traces through French to Latin fallere, to deceive.
latinIntro.cn: failure 经由法语追溯到拉丁语 fallere（欺骗）。

items.meaning: lack of success or a breakdown

items.exampleCN: 她始终如一的善意帮助了我们。

items.meaning: safe even if a part fails
items.example: The reactor has a fail-safe design.
items.exampleCN: 反应堆采用故障安全设计。

items.meaning: the heart's inability to pump properly
items.exampleCN: 心力衰竭需要谨慎治疗。

items.example: The power failure lasted an hour.
The failure rate fell after the fix.

latinEntries.example: Fallere is the source of fail and false.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fallere 是 fail 与 false 的源头。

definition_zh: 公平的；白皙的；合理的；集市；博览会
definition_en: treating people equally and according to the rules; light in colour; reasonable and acceptable; a market or exhibition
core_image: 天平两端放得一样平，谁也不多占一点
scene: 裁判必须公平对待双方。The referee must be fair to both sides.
sceneCN: 这里 fair 是「公平的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：裁判必须公平对待双方。

senses.title: Treating people equally
senses.definition: treating people equally and according to the rules
senses.definitionCN: 一视同仁并按规定行事
senses.example: The judge was fair to everyone.
senses.why: The core sense is balance between competing sides.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是竞争双方之间的平衡。

senses.title: Light in colour
senses.definition: light in colour, especially hair or skin
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浅，尤指头发或皮肤
senses.example: The child has fair hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子有一头浅色头发。
senses.why: The old sense of beautiful or bright survives in colour.
senses.whyCN: 古老「美丽、明亮」之义残留在颜色上。

senses.title: Reasonable
senses.definition: reasonable and acceptable, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 合理可接受，虽不算出色
senses.example: We paid a fair price for the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我们以合理的价格买了这辆车。
senses.why: A balanced deal is a fair deal.
senses.whyCN: 平衡的交易就是公平交易。

senses.title: A market or exhibition
senses.definition: a public event with stalls, amusements, or goods for sale
senses.definitionCN: 设有摊位、游乐设施或商品出售的公共活动
senses.example: The village fair opens every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的集市每年春天开市。
senses.why: The noun comes from a separate Latin word for a holiday.
senses.whyCN: 该名词来自另一个表示节日的拉丁词。

intro.en: Fair as an adjective comes from Old English fæger; the market sense comes from Latin feria, a holiday.
intro.cn: 形容词 fair 来自古英语 fæger；集市义则来自拉丁语 feria（节日）。

items.en: Fæger means beautiful or pleasant.
items.cn: fæger 意为美丽的、宜人的。

items.en: Fair develops the sense of just and equal.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fair 发展出公正平等之义。

items.en: Feria means a festival day.
items.cn: feria 意为节日。

items.en: Feire names a market or festival.
items.cn: feire 指集市或节庆。

items.en: Trade fair keeps the market sense alive.
items.cn: trade fair 使集市义延续至今。

note.en: Fair means just or light; fare is the price of a journey.
note.cn: fair 是公平或浅色，fare 则是车费。

entries.definition: the money paid for a journey

normalIntro.en: Fair covers justice, light colour, a reasonable deal, and a lively market.
normalIntro.cn: fair 涵盖公正、浅色、合理交易与热闹集市。

normal.en: Everyone deserves a fair trial.
normal.cn: 每个人都应得到公正的审判。

normal.en: The rules must be fair to all players.
normal.cn: 规则必须对所有选手公平。

normal.en: She has fair skin and dark eyes.
That is a fair question.
We visited the book fair on Sunday.

abstract.en: Picture a scale perfectly level on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两边完全水平的天平。

abstract.en: Imagine sunlight falling on pale hair.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光照在浅色头发上。

abstract.en: Think of a field full of colourful stalls.
abstract.cn: 想象满是彩色摊位的场地。

examples.en: It is not fair to blame her.
examples.cn: 责怪她是不公平的。

examples.en: They agreed on a fair price.
examples.cn: 他们商定了一个合理的价格。

examples.en: The science fair attracted many students.
examples.cn: 科学展吸引了许多学生。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 双源同形
dict_mnemonic.text: 形容词 fair（公平、浅色）是英语本族词；名词 fair（集市）来自拉丁语 feria（节日），两义同形不同源。

root: 形容词 fair 源自古英语 fæger（美丽的、宜人的），引申为公正与浅色；集市义另来自拉丁语 feria（节日）。

sensesIntro.en: Fair means just, light in colour, reasonable, or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: fair 意为公正、浅色、合理，或集市博览会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with equal weight on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：两端等重的天平。

branches.en: The base sense is equal treatment.
branches.cn: 基础义是平等对待。

branches.en: Brightness survives as light colour.
branches.cn: 明亮义留存为浅色。

branches.en: A balanced deal is reasonable.
branches.cn: 平衡的交易就是合理的。

branches.en: The market sense comes from another root.
branches.cn: 集市义来自另一词根。

branches.en: Justice and fair prices share one balance.
branches.cn: 公正与公道的价格共享同一种平衡。

intro.en: Fair builds fairness and fairly, and pairs with un- for unfair.
intro.cn: fair 构成 fairness 与 fairly，并与 un- 组合成 unfair。

latinIntro.en: The market sense comes from Latin feria, but the adjective is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 集市义来自拉丁语 feria，但形容词义属日耳曼语。

items.meaning: just, pale, reasonable, or a market

items.example: She was the fairest in the tale.
The trade fair opens on Monday.
Fair play is the spirit of the game.
items.exampleCN: 公平竞争是这项运动的精神。

latinEntries.example: Feria gives the market sense of fair.
latinEntries.exampleCN: feria 给出 fair 的集市义。

definition_en: to a moderate degree, quite; in a just and equal way; in a way that is deserved or according to the rules
core_image: 把强度调到中等，也把天平摆平
scene: 这部电影相当有趣。The film is fairly interesting.
sceneCN: 这里 fairly 是「相当地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这部电影相当有趣。

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to a moderate degree, more than a little but not very
senses.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，不止一点但不算很
senses.example: The test was fairly easy.
senses.why: The base sense here is a moderate level.
senses.whyCN: 此基础义是中等水平。

senses.title: In a just way
senses.definition: in a way that treats people equally and honestly
senses.definitionCN: 以平等诚实对待他人的方式
senses.example: The workers were treated fairly.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们受到了公平对待。
senses.why: The adverb applies the justice sense of fair.
senses.whyCN: 该副词落实 fair 的公正义。

senses.title: By right
senses.definition: in a way that is deserved or allowed by the rules
senses.definitionCN: 以应得或符合规则的方式
senses.example: They fairly earned their place in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凭实力正当地进入了决赛。
senses.why: A fair result is one that is deserved.
senses.whyCN: 公平的结果就是应得的结果。

intro.en: Fairly is fair plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: fairly 由 fair 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Fæger means beautiful or pleasant.
items.cn: fæger 意为美丽的、宜人的。

items.en: Fair gains the sense of just.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fair 获得公正之义。

items.en: Fairly means in a just manner.
items.cn: 十六世纪 fairly 意为以公正方式。

items.en: Fairly develops the sense of quite.
items.cn: 十九世纪 fairly 发展出「相当」之义。

items.en: Fairly often softens an opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fairly 常用来缓和评价。

note.en: Fairly means quite; fairy means a magical being.
note.cn: fairly 是相当地，fairy 则是仙女。

entries.definition: to a moderate or large degree
in a fair and sensible way

normalIntro.en: Fairly can soften a word or make it just.
normalIntro.cn: fairly 既能缓和语气，也能表达公正。

normal.en: The room was fairly clean.
I am fairly sure she will agree.
The staff treated us fairly.
normal.cn: 工作人员公平地对待我们。

normal.en: The match was fairly played.
He fairly deserved the award.

abstract.en: Picture a dial set halfway, not high or low.
abstract.cn: 想象旋钮停在中间，不高也不低。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale kept level by an honest hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只诚实的手让天平保持水平。

abstract.en: Think of a prize that was earned, not given.
abstract.cn: 想象一个挣来的、而非白给的奖。

examples.en: The instructions are fairly simple.
examples.cn: 说明相当简单。

examples.en: Every complaint should be fairly examined.
examples.cn: 每一起投诉都应得到公平审查。

examples.en: She fairly won the race.
examples.cn: 她正当地赢得了比赛。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 后缀派生
dict_mnemonic.text: fair（公平的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= fairly，既可表「公平地」，也可表「相当地」。

root: fairly 由 fair（公平的、合理的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源自古英语 fæger。

sensesIntro.en: Fairly means to a moderate degree, justly, or deservedly.
sensesIntro.cn: fairly 意为相当地、公平地，或正当地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level scale and a middle setting on a dial.
core.cn: 核心意象：水平的天平与居中的旋钮。

branches.en: The base sense here is a moderate degree.
branches.cn: 此基础义是中等程度。

branches.en: The word applies justice to an action.
branches.cn: 该词把公正用于行动。

branches.en: A fair result is a deserved one.
branches.cn: 公平的结果就是应得的结果。

branches.en: Both reduce force: one in degree, one in judgment.
branches.cn: 两者都降低力度：一个在程度，一个在评判。

branches.en: Just treatment and fair reward go together.
branches.cn: 公正对待与公平回报相伴。

intro.en: The suffix -ly turns fair into an adverb with two main senses.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 把 fair 变成具有两个主要义项的副词。

latinIntro.en: Fairly has a Germanic root; only the market noun has Latin origin.
latinIntro.cn: fairly 属日耳曼词根，只有集市名词义源自拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 我们想要一个公平的决定。
有人提出了更公平的制度。
他们寻求最公平的解决方案。

items.example: We are fairly certain of the date.

latinEntries.example: Feria is unrelated to the adjective fair.
latinEntries.exampleCN: feria 与形容词 fair 无关。

definition_en: strong belief in a religion; firm trust in someone or something; a religion; loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
core_image: 在看不见终点时仍把手交给对方
scene: 我对她的判断有信心。I have faith in her judgement.
sceneCN: 这里 faith 是「信心、信任」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我对她的判断有信心。

senses.title: Religious belief
senses.definition: strong belief in a religion or in God
senses.definitionCN: 对宗教或上帝的坚定信仰
senses.example: Her faith gave her strength.
senses.why: The core sense is trust in what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是对不可见之物的信任。

senses.title: Firm trust
senses.definition: firm trust in a person, plan, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、计划或想法的坚定信任
senses.example: We have faith in the new manager.
senses.why: Religious trust extends to everyday confidence.
senses.whyCN: 宗教信任延伸到日常的信心。

senses.title: A religion
senses.definition: a particular religion or system of belief
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定宗教或信仰体系
senses.example: People of many faiths live here.
senses.exampleCN: 许多不同信仰的人住在这里。
senses.why: The belief becomes a named community.
senses.whyCN: 信仰变成有名号的群体。

senses.title: Loyalty
senses.definition: loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
senses.definitionCN: 在关系或承诺中的忠诚与诚实
senses.example: He kept faith with his old friends.
senses.why: Trust between people becomes a bond of honour.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的信任成为信义纽带。

intro.en: Faith comes from Old French feid, from Latin fides, trust.
intro.cn: faith 来自古法语 feid，源头是拉丁语 fides（信任）。

items.en: Fides means trust or faithfulness.
items.cn: fides 意为信任或忠诚。

items.en: Fidere means to trust.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任。

items.en: Feid carries the sense of loyalty.
items.cn: feid 带有忠诚之义。

items.en: Faith means belief and promise.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faith 兼指信念与承诺。

items.en: Faith covers religion and personal trust.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faith 涵盖宗教与个人信任。

note.en: Faith is trust; fate is destiny.
note.cn: faith 是信任，fate 则是命运。

entries.definition: the feeling that something is true
a system of worship and belief

normalIntro.en: Faith is trust that holds even when proof is missing.
normalIntro.cn: faith 是在缺少证据时仍然坚持的信任。

normal.en: She never lost faith in her team.
normal.cn: 她从未对团队失去信心。

normal.en: They acted in good faith.
People of different faiths prayed together.
normal.cn: 不同信仰的人一起祈祷。

normal.en: He kept faith with his promise.
It was an act of faith to start the business.
normal.cn: 创办这家企业是一种信念之举。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching out in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中伸出的手。

abstract.en: Imagine a promise kept without witnesses.
abstract.cn: 想象没有见证人时仍守住的承诺。

abstract.en: Think of a light you trust before you see it.
abstract.cn: 把信仰想成一盏尚未看见却相信的灯。

examples.en: Her faith in people remained strong.
examples.cn: 她对人的信心依然坚定。

examples.en: The treaty was signed in good faith.
examples.cn: 条约是本着善意签署的。

examples.en: Patients need faith in their doctor.
examples.cn: 病人需要信任自己的医生。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: faith 与 fidelity、confide 同源于拉丁语 fides（信任），核心就是「信」。

root: faith 经由古法语 feid 来自拉丁语 fides（信任、忠诚），与 fidelity、confide 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Faith is religious belief, firm trust, a religion, or loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: faith 指宗教信仰、坚定信任、某宗教，或忠诚信义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: trust offered without visible proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：在看不见证据时给予的信任。

branches.en: The base sense is trust in the unseen.
branches.cn: 基础义是对不可见之物的信任。

branches.en: Trust extends to people and plans.
branches.cn: 信任延伸到人与计划。

branches.en: The belief becomes a named religion.
branches.cn: 信仰变成有名号的宗教。

branches.en: Trust between people becomes loyalty.
branches.cn: 人与人之间的信任成为忠诚。

branches.en: Religious faith and personal honour both keep promises.
branches.cn: 宗教信仰与个人信义都守承诺。

intro.en: Faith builds faithful, faithfully, and faithless.
intro.cn: faith 构成 faithful、faithfully 与 faithless。

latinIntro.en: Latin fides and fidere explain faith and its Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fides 与 fidere 解释了 faith 及其拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 这座城市欢迎所有宗教。

items.example: He was faithless to his word.
The claim was made in bad faith.
We must keep faith with voters.

latinEntries.example: Fides is the root of faith.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fides 是 faith 的词根。
fidere 是 confide 的前身。

definition_zh: 落下；下降；跌倒；进入某种状态；秋天
definition_en: to move downward under gravity; to decrease in amount or level; to lose balance and go down; to pass into a state; the season of autumn
core_image: 一片叶子离开枝头，旋转着落向地面
scene: 秋天树叶纷纷落下。Leaves fall from the trees in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 fall 是「落下」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秋天树叶纷纷落下。

senses.title: To move downward
senses.definition: to move downward under the force of gravity
senses.definitionCN: 在重力作用下向下移动
senses.example: The leaves fall in October.
senses.why: The core sense is the pull of gravity.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是重力的拉扯。

senses.title: To decrease
senses.definition: to decrease in amount, level, or value
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或价值下降
senses.example: Prices fell sharply last month.
senses.why: A falling number moves down like a falling object.
senses.whyCN: 下降的数字像下落的物体一样走低。

senses.title: To lose balance
senses.definition: to lose balance and go down to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 失去平衡倒向地面
senses.example: He fell on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的小路上摔倒了。
senses.why: The body drops when it can no longer stand.
senses.whyCN: 身体无法站稳时就会倒下。

senses.title: To pass into a state
senses.definition: to pass suddenly into a particular state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 突然进入某种状态或状况
senses.example: The baby fell asleep in her arms.
senses.why: Falling into a state is like dropping into it.
senses.whyCN: 「落入」某种状态就像掉进去。

senses.title: Autumn
senses.definition: the season between summer and winter, especially in American English; also an act of falling
senses.definitionCN: 夏冬之间的季节，尤用于美式英语；也指下落的行为
senses.example: The leaves turn gold in the fall.
senses.why: The season is named for the falling of leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这个季节因落叶而得名。

intro.en: Fall comes from Old English feallan; the autumn sense comes from the fall of the leaf.
intro.cn: fall 源自古英语 feallan；秋天义来自「落叶时节」的说法。

items.en: A common root means to fall.
items.cn: 共同的词根意为落下。

items.en: Feallan means to drop down.
items.cn: feallan 意为落下。

items.en: Fall develops figurative senses.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fall 发展出比喻义。

items.en: The fall of the leaf names autumn.
items.cn: the fall of the leaf 用来指秋天。

items.en: Fall becomes the usual word for autumn.
items.cn: 美式英语中 fall 成为秋天的常用词。

note.en: Fall means to drop; fail means to not succeed.
note.cn: fall 是落下，fail 则是失败。

normalIntro.en: Fall covers gravity, numbers, bodies, states, and the autumn season.
normalIntro.cn: fall 涵盖重力、数字、身体、状态与秋季。

normal.en: Rain fell all night.
The temperature fell below zero.
She fell down the stairs.
He fell asleep during the film.
We visit the farm every fall.
normal.cn: 我们每年秋天都去农场。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf letting go of its branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子松开树枝。

abstract.en: Imagine a number sliding down a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象数字沿图表下滑。

abstract.en: Think of a body folding gently to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象身体轻轻倒向地面。

examples.en: Snow began to fall at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时开始下雪。

examples.en: Sales fell by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额下降了百分之十。

examples.en: The old tree fell in the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨中那棵老树倒了。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 本族词
dict_mnemonic.text: fall 是英语本族词；美式英语用 the fall 表示「秋天」，因为这是树叶飘落的季节。

root: fall 源自古英语 feallan（落下），属日耳曼语族；秋天义来自 the fall of the leaf（落叶时节）。

sensesIntro.en: Fall means to drop, decrease, tumble, enter a state, or the season of autumn.
sensesIntro.cn: fall 意为落下、下降、跌倒、进入某状态，或秋天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf letting go and drifting down.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶子松开枝头飘落。

branches.en: The base sense is downward movement.
branches.cn: 基础义是向下移动。

branches.en: Numbers and values move down too.
branches.cn: 数字与价值也会走低。

branches.en: A body that loses balance falls.
branches.cn: 失去平衡的身体会倒下。

branches.en: States are entered as if by falling into them.
branches.cn: 状态像是掉进去一样被进入。

branches.en: The season is named for falling leaves.
branches.cn: 这个季节因落叶得名。

intro.en: Fall forms compounds such as waterfall and phrasal verbs such as fall down.
intro.cn: fall 构成 waterfall 等复合词与 fall down 等短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Fall is a Germanic word with no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: fall 是日耳曼词，没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to drop or the act of dropping
items.example: The cup fell from the table.
The apple fell to the ground.
The fallen leaves covered the path.
The waterfall is fifty metres high.

items.exampleCN: 这场争端造成了严重后果。
我们需要一个备用方案。

definition_zh: 错误的；假的；不忠实的；虚伪的
definition_en: not true or correct; not genuine but made to look real; not loyal or sincere; based on a mistaken idea
core_image: 一件外表逼真、内里却空心的仿制品
scene: 那只是一场虚惊。It was only a false alarm.
sceneCN: 这里 false 是「错误的、虚假的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那只是一场虚惊。

senses.title: Not true
senses.definition: not true or correct
senses.definitionCN: 不真实或不正确的
senses.example: The rumour turned out to be false.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传言最终被证明是假的。
senses.why: The core sense is a statement that does not match facts.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是与事实不符的说法。

senses.title: Not genuine
senses.definition: not genuine but made to look real
senses.definitionCN: 并非真品，却做得像真的
senses.example: He gave a false name to the police.
senses.why: A copy pretends to be the real thing.
senses.whyCN: 仿制品假装是真品。

senses.title: Not loyal
senses.definition: not loyal or sincere toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人不忠诚或不真诚
senses.example: A false friend leaves when trouble comes.
senses.exampleCN: 假朋友在麻烦来临时就会离开。
senses.why: A person can also be a hollow copy of a friend.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可能是朋友的虚假复制品。

senses.title: Based on a mistake
senses.definition: based on a mistaken idea or wrong belief
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误观念或错误信念上
senses.example: The locked door gave them a false sense of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 锁上的门给了他们一种虚假的安全感。
senses.why: A wrong belief is a false map of reality.
senses.whyCN: 错误信念是现实的假地图。

intro.en: False comes from Latin falsus, deceived or deceptive, from fallere, to deceive.
intro.cn: false 来自拉丁语 falsus（被欺骗的、欺骗性的），源头 fallere（欺骗）。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗。

items.en: Falsus means false or deceptive.
items.cn: falsus 意为虚假的或欺骗性的。

items.en: Fals carries the same sense.
items.cn: fals 带有相同含义。

items.en: False means untrue and disloyal.
items.cn: 中古英语中 false 意为不真实与不忠。

items.en: False also describes artificial things.
items.cn: 现代英语中 false 也描述人造之物。

note.en: False means untrue; fault is a mistake or defect.
note.cn: false 是虚假的，fault 则是过错或缺陷。

normalIntro.en: False covers untrue claims, fake objects, disloyal people, and mistaken beliefs.
normalIntro.cn: false 涵盖不实说法、假货、不忠之人与错误信念。

normal.en: The story was completely false.
He travelled under a false name.
She accused him of false promises.
normal.cn: 她指责他许下虚假的承诺。

normal.en: The alarm was false, so we went back inside.
normal.cn: 警报是误报，所以我们又回去了。

normal.en: Test each statement as true or false.
normal.cn: 判断每个说法是真是假。

abstract.en: Picture a gold ring that leaves a green mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚留下绿痕的「金」戒指。

abstract.en: Imagine a sign pointing the wrong way.
abstract.cn: 想象一块指错方向的标牌。

abstract.en: Think of a friend who vanishes when needed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个需要时就消失的朋友。

examples.en: The witness gave false information.
examples.cn: 证人提供了虚假信息。

examples.en: He was accused of using a false passport.
examples.cn: 他被控使用假护照。

examples.en: Beware of false friends online.
examples.cn: 当心网络上的假朋友。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: false 与 fail、fault 同源于拉丁语 fallere（欺骗），凡是「骗人」的，都是 false。

root: false 源自拉丁语 falsus（虚假的），来自 fallere（欺骗），与 fail、fault 同族。

sensesIntro.en: False means untrue, not genuine, disloyal, or based on a mistaken belief.
sensesIntro.cn: false 意为不真实、非真品、不忠诚，或基于错误观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a convincing shell with nothing real inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：外表可信、内里空空的壳。

branches.en: The base sense is not matching the facts.
branches.cn: 基础义是与事实不符。

branches.en: A fake object pretends to be real.
branches.cn: 假货假装是真品。

branches.en: A disloyal person is a hollow friend.
branches.cn: 不忠之人是空心的朋友。

branches.en: A wrong belief is a false map.
branches.cn: 错误信念是假地图。

branches.en: False words and false goods both deceive.
branches.cn: 假话与假货都在骗人。

intro.en: False builds nouns and adverbs with -hood, -ity, and -ly.
intro.cn: false 通过 -hood、-ity 与 -ly 构成名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin falsus, fallere, and falsitas explain false and its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus、fallere 与 falsitas 解释了 false 及其词族。

items.example: They proved the falsity of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 他们证明了这个说法的虚假。

items.example: The report was full of falsehoods.

items.meaning: a warning that turns out to be untrue
items.example: The fire was a false alarm.
She booked the room under a false name.
